title: BGN regime-gamma with RARE, short stress (10% of months)
question: Can a complexity method learn a regime interaction from a window holding only a few stress months?
notes:
B1-rare. Changes BOTH switch probabilities AND the stationary mix: p01 0.05/12, p10 0.45/12, so stress is 10% of months instead of 33%, with calm spells of 240 months and stress spells of 27. gmult unchanged at [0.2, 3.5]. Unlike g0235f/g0235s this is a DIFFERENT economy, not the same one at a different speed: the stationary mix moves, so the premia and the ceilings move with it. This is the crash-like calibration -- rare, severe, short -- and the question is a small-sample one: a 360-month window holds about 36 stress months, so the regime interaction must be learned from a tenth of the data. PREDICTION: room falls (less time spent in the high-price regime), and the gap falls further because DKKM's advantage here is an interaction it now has few observations of. A gap that HOLDS UP would be the strong result, since rare-and-severe is the empirically defensible shape.
